definition: Utilization-focused evaluation is an approach to evaluation that centers on the needs and values of the people who will use the findings. In the source, it is described as a way to examine and improve practice by gathering users’ perspectives and identifying strengths and challenges that can guide practical changes.

reasons: The definition adds that the approach identifies “strengths and challenges” to guide practical changes; the source supports identifying a strength (communication) and optimizing practice, but it does not explicitly support identifying challenges in this way.
The field “biological” is not defensible from the packet; the source concerns evaluation in an inclusive sailing team, not biology.
The definition’s first sentence is supported: the packet states the evaluation followed the Patton approach of utilization-focused evaluation, which places users’ needs and values at the center.

The second sentence includes claims not fully supported by the packet: it mentions gathering users’ perspectives (supported by interviews) but also says it identifies “strengths and challenges” and that these “guide practical changes,” while the packet text explicitly reports identifying a “strength” (communication) and does not clearly state “challenges” or that the findings directly guided specific practical changes.

The packet text does not support the broader, generic phrasing that “utilization-focused evaluation” is described in the source as a general mechanism involving strengths and challenges guiding practical changes; the evidence provided is limited to the described project outcomes.
